subject: construction of figure urls given fig.path, base.url, and base.dir?

messages.author: 30b406a9189eeb25
messages.subject: construction of figure urls given fig.path, base.url, and base.dir?
parts:
Hi list,

I am a bit confused as to the construction of relative URLs used to link markdown figures.  In particular, I find the website documentation of `base.url` and `base.dir` very vague.  

Imagine I have a .Rmd file in a working directory named `docs/` and that a sister directory exists along side it called `docs-gh-pages`.  

If I specify:

    opts_knit$set(base.url = "/docs/", base.dir="../docs-gh-pages/")
    opts_chunk$set(fig.path="figures/")

Then I think that the figure is written in the path defined relative to my R _working directory_, `"../docs-gh-pages/figures/fig-name.png"`, while the figure is embedded in the markdown as: 

    ![figure caption](/docs/figures/fig-name.png)

Which is what I would expect: the figure URL composed of the `base.url` and `fig.path` concatenated, and the figure written to the local path created by concatenating `base.dir` and `fig.path`.  Is this correct? 

If I specify: 


    opts_knit$set(base.url = "/docs/", base.dir=".")
    opts_chunk$set(fig.path = "../docs-gh-pages/figures/")


I would expect this to then generate the same end result, but instead no figure is rendered (and indeed no markdown output appears following the plot command, and no error message appears in the markdown or the console.  

Confused,
Carl



--
Carl Boettiger
UC Santa Cruz

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] construction of figure urls given fig.path, base.url, and base.dir?
parts:
Yes, I agree these options are confusing. base.dir is never used when
composing the URL of the figures; it is only used to save the figures
to a different directory, which can be useful when you do not wan the
figures to be saved under the current working directory. The URL of an
image is always base.url + fig.path.

Regards,
Yihui
--
Yihui Xie <xiey...@gmail.com>
Web: http://yihui.name
